The investigated samples were GaN thin layers with embedded ferromagnetic γ'-Ga_y Fe_4-y N nanocrystals, fabricated by metal organic vapor phase epitaxy.
The nanocrystals had a size range of (17±8) nm along the c-growth direction and (50±20) nm to (20±8) nm in the layer plane.
The nanocrystal density was tunable from 3.9 × 10^9 to 15.0 × 10^9 NC/cm^2 by adjusting the Ga supply during growth.
The lattice parameter of the nanocrystals along the c-growth direction increased from 3.789 Å to 3.806 Å as the Ga content increased.
The Ga atoms preferred to occupy the 3c Wyckoff sites in the fcc structure of the nanocrystals, rather than the 1a sites.
The maximum Ga occupancy in the 3c sites of the nanocrystals was around 30%.
The normalized magnetization and Curie temperature (T_C) of the nanocrystals showed an inverse correlation with the amount of Ga in the 3c sites.
The T_C of the nanocrystals ranged from 450K to 500K as the Ga content increased.
In contrast to the weakly antiferromagnetic behavior reported for γ'-GaFe_3N powders, the γ'-Ga_y Fe_4-y N nanocrystals remained ferromagnetic up to 30% Ga content in the 3c sites.

The combination of AXD and DAFS at the Ga K-edge allowed the researchers to selectively probe the Ga atoms in the nanocrystals and quantify their incorporation, even in the presence of the Ga-containing GaN matrix.
The ferromagnetic properties of the γ'-Ga_y Fe_4-y N nanocrystals make them promising for applications in magnetic data storage, spin current generation, and spintronic devices.
The researchers found that by adjusting the growth parameters, the Ga atoms could be induced to incorporate into the 3c positions at the faces of the fcc crystal lattice of the nanocrystals.
The DAFS technique was crucial in this study, as it allowed the researchers to distinguish the contribution of Ga atoms in the nanocrystals from the Ga atoms in the surrounding GaN matrix.

The quantitative analysis of the DAFS data showed that the ideal crystallographic structure of the nanocrystals was slightly distorted, with the two groups of next-nearest neighbors found at positions slightly different from the natural ones.
The researchers were able to correlate the fabrication parameters, local crystallographic arrangement, and overall magnetic properties of the material system.
